80 years of the UN Security Council

Understanding the Security Council through its resolutions: patterns in themes, voting and language since 1946, drawn from every resolution, vote and veto. Every figure is counted from the documents.

What stands out

01The Council went from recommending to ordering

"Decides" appears in 20% of resolutions in the founding era and 96% since 2022. "Acting under Chapter VII" went from about 1% of resolutions before 1988 to 50%.

Read the full analysis
02The vocabulary of war changed

"Aggression" peaked in 1975 to 1987, mostly about South Africa, then all but disappeared. "Breach of the peace" was found for only four wars, the last in 1990. "Threat to the peace" became the routine trigger: 2% of resolutions in the founding era, 55% today.

Read the full analysis
03The veto map flipped twice

The USSR cast most vetoes until 1960, the United States from the 1970s to the 1990s, Russia and China since 2011. 270 drafts have been vetoed since 1946.

Read the full analysis
04Unity rose and is now falling

Unanimous adoption climbed from 39% in the founding years to 93% in 2001 to 2010, then fell to 61% in 2025. On contested votes the US and Russia now agree 8% of the time, against 57% around 1990.

Read the full analysis
05From wars between states to wars inside them

Civilians, women, children and sexual violence were almost absent before 1999. Women now appear in 59% of resolutions and civilians in 38%. The median resolution grew from 234 words in 1960 to 1974 to 1,865 in 2011 to 2021.

Read the full analysis
06Africa took over the agenda

Africa went from 0% of resolutions in the founding era to 52% in 2011 to 2021.

Read the full analysis

At a glance

The Council adopted about 9 resolutions a year in its first era and over 60 a year from 1994 to 2010. Output has fallen every year since 2021, to 44 in 2025, the lowest since 1991. The quiet years of the Cold War were divided years: unanimity often sat below half.

The eight eras

The periods follow political breaks, not decades. Each break shows in the data: a jump in output, a change in unanimity, a new veto caster or new words.

EraOpened byPer yearUnanimousWhat the documents show
1946 to 1959
Founding and early Cold War		The UN starts work939%Palestine, Kashmir, Indonesia, Korea. 25% of resolutions concern admissions, elections or appointments. The USSR casts 89 of the 95 vetoes and 65 drafts fail for lack of votes. Palestine 1948 (54 (1948)) is the first "threat to the peace" finding, Korea 1950 (82 (1950)) the first "breach of the peace".
1960 to 1974
Decolonisation		17 African states admitted in 1960; Council enlarged to 15 in 19651657%Africa rises to 27% of resolutions. First mandatory sanctions, on Southern Rhodesia (232 (1966)). First "Acting under Chapter VII" (253 (1968)). The UK casts 10 vetoes; the US casts its first in 1970.
1975 to 1987
Late Cold War		End of the Portuguese empire, wars in Southern Africa and Lebanon1856%The "aggression" era: the word appears in 14% of resolutions, most of them about South Africa. Apartheid appears in 8%. The US becomes the main veto caster (50), with the UK (17) and France (11).
1988 to 1993
Thaw and boom		Iran and Iraq ceasefire (598, 1987), end of the Cold War4880%Output rises to 48 a year, peaking at 93 resolutions in 1993. Kuwait 1990 (660 (1990)) is the last "breach of the peace"; 678 (1990) authorises "all necessary means". Europe, mostly the former Yugoslavia, reaches 26%.
1994 to 2000
Humanitarian wars and failures		Rwanda genocide, war in Bosnia6386%Africa 38%, Europe 26%. "Humanitarian" in 46%. A tribunal for Rwanda (955 (1994)). Protection of civilians becomes an agenda item (1265 (1999)). Only 7 drafts are vetoed.
2001 to 2010
Terror, robust peacekeeping, thematic agendas		9/11, the women and peace agenda (1325, 2000)6393%Peak unity: 93% unanimous. Chapter VII in 44% of resolutions. Terrorism becomes a general threat (1373 (2001)). Women in 23%, justice and impunity in 38%. Africa 48%.
2011 to 2021
From Libya to Syria		Libya intervention 2011, Syria vetoes from October 20115988%Longest texts (median 1,865 words). Sanctions in 45%, women in 59%, civilians in 38%. Russia (22) and China (11) lead the vetoes. The US and Russia vote alike on 14% of contested votes.
2022 to 2026
Ukraine and fragmentation		Russia's invasion of Ukraine4466%Output falls to 44 a year; 2025 has 44, the lowest since 1991. Middle East 20%, the Americas (mostly Haiti) 10%. Russia (13) and the US (9) lead the vetoes. The one adopted Ukraine resolution (2774 (2025)) speaks of a "conflict", with no finding of aggression or breach.

New to the Security Council?

The basics in five boxes. Read the full explainer.

What it isThe UN's body for peace and securityAll UN members agree to carry out its decisions (Article 25 of the Charter). Who sits on it15 members, 5 permanentChina, France, Russia, the United Kingdom and the United States, plus ten members elected for two years. How it decidesNine votes and no vetoA single no from a permanent member blocks a draft. 270 drafts have been vetoed since 1946. What it can doRecommend, or orderChapter VI to settle disputes; Chapter VII for sanctions, peace operations and the use of force. What a resolution is2,835 decisions, numbered since 1946Browse every resolution with its full text, vote and citations.

Security Council Record is an independent record of every resolution, vote and veto of the United Nations Security Council since 1946. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by the United Nations. For official documents, use the Security Council website and the UN Digital Library.

Built on the documentation of the Security Council, the CR-UNSC corpus (Fobbe, Gasbarri and Ridi, CC0), the UN machine-readable resolutions and the UNSC votes since 1946 database (Sciences Po Atelier de cartographie and GRAM, CC BY 4.0). Method and sources.
